question: A hospital policy requires HIV testing for all patients before any surgical procedure, without obtaining the patient's explicit consent. Under the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act 2017, this policy is:

answers.text: Legal, because pre-operative HIV screening is a standard infection control measure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The HIV Act 2017 explicitly prohibits mandatory HIV testing. Infection control rationale does not override the legal requirement for informed consent before HIV testing.

answers.text: Illegal — mandatory HIV testing without informed consent is specifically prohibited under the HIV Act 2017

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Section 5 of the HIV Act 2017 prohibits mandatory HIV testing. Every HIV test requires pre-test counselling and informed consent. Mandatory pre-operative testing without consent violates the Act.

answers.text: Legal only if the patient is unconscious or unable to consent, as a standard-of-care protocol

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Emergency treatment for an unconscious patient may proceed without consent, but this does not extend to mandatory HIV testing. The Act's prohibition applies regardless of clinical setting.

answers.text: Permitted as 'opt-out' testing, since the patient is informed during pre-operative assessment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Partially: opt-out testing may be more permissible than mandatory testing in some contexts, but must still include pre-test counselling and a genuine opportunity to decline. A blanket policy without individual counselling violates the Act.

overallFeedback.feedback: Mandatory HIV testing is illegal under the HIV Act 2017. Every test requires informed consent with pre-test counselling. This applies in all clinical settings including pre-operative.
Correct. The HIV Act 2017 prohibits mandatory HIV testing. Informed consent is required before every HIV test. Pre-operative blanket testing policies without consent are illegal.
